transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 50 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa (Redwood AE), Kai (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM); Jonah (Veridian ML), Priya (SRE), Dmitri (Security), Sara (Product), Sam (Intern)

Auto-summary: go/no-go criteria narrowed, focus on model fencing, KMS questions outstanding, agree to two benchmark runs and a tabletop rollback drill.

00:00 Alyssa: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, 50 minutes on the clock. quick roll call?
00:08 Jonah: Jonah here, ready
00:10 Priya: Priya here
00:12 Dmitri: Dmitri here
00:13 Sara: Sara here
00:15 Kai: Kai here from Redwood
00:18 Maya: Maya here, CSM
00:20 Alyssa: cool, agenda — share last week's perf, propose pin matrix, decide fallback runbook, security q's, action items. any other items?
00:30 Sara: just want to reiterate user impact for the triage flow — sub-200ms tail is, like, ideal for 20% of traffic.
00:40 Alyssa: yes, we kept that in mind; Kai, can you walk through the latest numbers?
00:45 Kai: sure, um the test suite we ran last night — approximate numbers: rw-instruct-3 (quantized q4) median p50 ~110ms, p95 ~300ms on 4xA10 pool; Llama-3 mid ~p50 95ms p95 420ms on same config; Mistral-lite variant sits in between. important caveat: the Llama-3 numbers had slightly smaller batch sizes in the run, so p95 a bit inflated—we're working to normalize.
01:25 Jonah: wait real quick, Llama-3 at 95ms p50 but 420 p95? that variance is scary for us. is KV cache warm in that run?
01:33 Kai: partially warmed, yes. we saw spikes when cold-starts hit, which inflates the p95. prefix caching would cut that in half for repeated user sessions, but for sporadic triage requests you still see occasional tails.
01:48 Priya: our traffic is bursty, so cold-start behavior matters. also cost — what's the token cost delta between rw-instruct-3 q4 and Llama-3 non-quant?
01:58 Kai: rough delta: Llama-3 raw cost ~1.3x vs rw-instruct quantized, but with batching and cache the effective cost gap narrows; full estimates in the pin matrix I'll send.
02:10 Sara: can you also add inference time variance per seq length? we triage sometimes send longer context (up to 1024 tokens) — need to see tail behavior at 1k.
02:20 Kai: yes will annotate that.
02:25 Alyssa: switching to the pin matrix proposal — we recommended locked variants for the pilot: rw-instruct-3-q4 as primary for triage, Llama-3-lite as soft fallback, and a smaller opt-in high-accuracy model for escalation. Kai walk through the gating windows.
02:40 Kai: policy idea: pin at the route-level for two weeks with a 48-hour golden canary before rolling; soft fallback mapping by error rate and latency breach. for example: if p95 > 350ms for three consecutive 5-minute windows, route to Llama-3-lite or to dedicated pool with more GPUs.
03:05 Dmitri: from security, we need to ensure any fallback to a dedicated pool still enforces VPC peering and KMS keys — can't have keys leave the HSM boundary. are we confident the routing preserves KMS usage?
03:18 Kai: yes, routing is at the control plane layer and we keep envelope encryption intact; for private deployment we can insist on customer KMS passthrough. note: some older kernels had an issue with key wrapping, but that's fixed in the 2025-05 runtime.
03:42 Dmitri: do you have a KB article or a short doc? I don't want to rely on verbal assurances.
03:48 Alyssa: yes, we'll share the KMS integration guide and a runbook excerpt.
03:52 Maya: quick note on telemetry — we'll propagate token-level latencies to your dashboard so you can alert on p95.
03:58 Priya: good. also need audit log granularity — per-request headers for PHI audit.
04:05 Maya: audit logs include request id, model variant, route, and who triggered the key. we can bump retention on enterprise plan — details in security appendix.
04:20 Sara: on rollbacks/why: if we see hallucination regression after a model push, what's the fast cutover? how long to rollback?
04:30 Kai: immediate soft rollback is weight-shifted traffic: we do 100% redirect in under 60s at the control plane level; downstream caches might flush in 2mins. for staged unpinning we recommend a 10-minute rollback window with automated health checks.
04:55 Jonah: can you describe the health checks? are they purely latency, or also quality?
05:03 Kai: both — latency SLOs, error rate, and a small synthetic eval set (our smoke tests) that runs every minute on a shadow copy. if synthetic eval degrades past threshold, automatic drain to fallback. caveat: synthetic tests sometimes have false positives; hence the 2-step canary.
05:30 Alyssa: let's talk about cost impact — if we use dedicated pools as fallback for hot periods, what's the monthly delta?
05:39 Kai: ballpark: moving 20% of traffic to dedicated medium pool increases monthly by ~15-25% depending on utilization and reserved discounts; exacts in the cost sheet.
05:50 Sara: we need a tight number — finance needs a worst-case scenario.
05:54 Alyssa: I'll include both conservative and optimistic scenarios in the spreadsheet.
05:58 Priya: question on data residency — if fallback spins up in a different region, is data residency preserved?
06:06 Kai: routing respects customer region constraints; we can pin fallback pools to same region. for global failover we have to opt in and sign off on egress.
06:16 Dmitri: what about compliance — SOC 2 type 2 attestation and change logs for model swaps?
06:23 Maya: Redwood is submitting an updated SOC narrative for the POC; we'll attach the change log for model pin operations and an audit trail example.
06:30 Dmitri: need that before tabletop drill.
06:35 Alyssa: noted.
06:38 Jonah: one thing we observed in the last test — quantization sometimes increased halluc rate on one prompt cluster. do you have mitigation?
06:46 Kai: yes. mitigation is two-fold: targeted prompt rewrite and a fallback to non-quantized model for that prompt hash. we can also shadow test non-quantized on a small percentage to measure.
06:58 Sara: can we create a prompt-level override table? some prompts are super sensitive.
07:03 Kai: yes, we can map prompt hashes to model overrides in the routing config. will add examples.
07:10 Alyssa: next, bench plan: two short runs — one stability (1 hour steady at 50rps) and one burst (10m 400rps) — Jonah to run in staging; Kai will monitor and collect kv cache heatmaps.
07:26 Jonah: ok I'll run the jobs tomorrow morning; which config?
07:30 Kai: use rw-instruct-3-q4 primary, Llama-3-lite soft fallback, batching at 8 for production-like pattern; include cold-start intervals to simulate user churn.
07:45 Priya: ensure logs include request path and user-id hash for correlation.
07:50 Sam (intern): small question — do we keep the deprecated runtime 2025-04 in the pool?
07:55 Kai: we can keep it for rollback but recommend removing after we validate the RL fixes. it adds complexity.
08:03 Alyssa: timeline check — we're aiming for pilot cutover week of 2025-06-02, with a tabletop drill the week prior. sound right?
08:10 Sara: yes, product is aligned for that week pending the benches.
08:13 Dmitri: security needs SOC docs and KMS notes before 05-27 tabletop.
08:18 Alyssa: we'll get that to you by 05-21.
08:22 Maya: recap of action items and owners (see action items list).
08:30 Jonah: quick Q — any concerns about vendor lock if we pin hard to rw-instruct?
08:36 Alyssa: good question — the catalog keeps multiple open-models available; our routing supports multi-model pins to avoid lock-in. we'll document the escape hatches.
08:48 Jira/link refs: pin-matrix.xlsx (drive link), kms-integration.pdf (sec link), price-delta.xlsx (finance link)
08:55 Alyssa: ok thanks everyone, we'll share notes and runbook. next sync same time next week, unless we call the tabletop earlier.
09:02 meeting end

Notes about transcript quality: minor mis-hears (rw-instruct sometimes transcribed as re-instruct), occasional speaker mislabels.
